case: post-Phase-1 shared #248/#256 ownership substrate: indexed registry and work-driven reclamation
kind: count-driven diagnostic plus the existing functional owned-payload route; no timed phase and no cache-qualified measurement

source.note: payload_route.py read `git rev-parse HEAD` before this commit existed, so its `source` field names the first parent; the product_inputs_sha256 it recorded is recomputed here over the committed product source and is identical.

change.registry: State.records is BTreeMap<payload-id, Arc<Record>> in id order; by-id lookup is O(log N) and is what Arena::payload (one frozen Commit piece) and the cleanup frame's payload owner use
change.custody_ownership: RootState.custodies carries (PageRef, payload-id) so releasing custody is an indexed lookup, not a registry walk
change.routine_reclamation: PayloadHost keeps a release list; a record enters it when its last external OwnedPayload reference drops or its custody page is released, and maintain() drains that list instead of searching the registry
change.scoped_pass: reclaim(incarnation) keeps an ordered cursor over the registry and re-derives the aggregate admission flags once per pass, so releasing N owners costs O(N)
change.charged_registry: the registry is charged REGISTRY_ENTRY_BYTES = 32 per entry (map entry plus its share of a node) instead of the old doubling vector-capacity reserve
